industrial carbon emissions, but scaling to meet growing demand is contingent on having
sufficient space for renewable energy infrastructure. Assuming a scenario in which $10\%$ coverage
of currently eligible land by such infrastructure is feasible, researchers calculated a scarcity factor
(with values above 1 indicating insufficient land) for the United Kingdom, France, and China by
comparing the amount of land required for electricity production adequate to the country’s

projected 2050 demand for green hydrogen with the amount of available land. A student reviews

The scarcity factors imply that all three countries will produce more hydrogen per unit of land
by using only solar energy than by using only wind energy, which suggests that the solar
coverage scenario is more feasible than the wind coverage scenario; therefore, the student’s claim
is fully supported.

France has the lowest scarcity factor for wind among the three countries, suggesting that it will
likely need to supplement the use of wind energy with the use of solar energy; therefore, the
student’s claim is not supported for France but is for the United Kingdom and China.

The scarcity factors indicate that although France and China would have the capacity to use
only solar energy but not only wind energy to meet green hydrogen demands, the United
Kingdom would not have the capacity to meet demands using either solar or wind energy;

Rare species advantage (RSA) describes the situation in which there are few conspecifics (other
members of the same species) in an organism’s immediate surroundings, enabling the organism to
avoid competition with conspecifics for the same resources; RSA is widely believed to play a
crucial role in maintaining ecological stability. Among tree species in the Mo Singto plot (latitude
$14.26^{\circ}N)$ and other tropical forest sites, there is little correlation between conspecific aggregation
and the abundance of a given species in the wider local area, so RSA is expected, but in the
Smithsonian Conservation Biology Institute (latitude $38.89^{\circ}N)$ and other temperate forest sites,
the aggregation-abundance correlation for tree species is strongly negative. Mathematical
modeling suggests, however, that ecological niche distinction may mitigate the apparent risk to
temperate ecological stability engendered by this pattern: \_\_\_\_\_\_

prompt.text: Which choice most logically completes the text?

content.text:
although rare tree species in temperate forests encounter relatively high local competition from
conspecifics, they can thrive by exploiting resources that are underexploited by other local
species.

while an increase in abundance in one tree species often leads to a reduction in abundance of
nearby species, temperate tree species tend to play different roles in the same ecosystem, reducing
the expected effect of abundance on aggregation.

even though rare tree species in temperate forests tend to cluster with conspecifics more than
rare tree species in tropical forests do, they are sufficiently rare locally that they benefit from

as a tree species in temperate forests becomes more abundant, individuals of that species are
more likely to be found near conspecifics, enabling abundant species to exploit localized
resources to a greater extent than rare species can.
